In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charge disproportionation is the most important factor for the hyperfine interactions in nickelates in the temperature ranges of magnetic and structure transitions.

the hyperfine interactions of 59Co and 57Fe impurities in the nickelates YbNiO2.9 and TmNiO2.85, respectively, reflect the charge disproportionation and the localization of the electronic states in Ni3+ cation in the range of the insulator (T > TIM).

the hyperfine interaction of 57Fe probe nuclei is sensitive to the electronic structure of Ni3+ ions and the structural distortion of perovskite nickelate lattice in the ranges of the phase transitions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the charge disproportionation and the formation of the Ni3+ and Ni4+ cations in TmNi and YbNi are the key factors in the electronic localization of the nickelates in the temperature range of TIM.
the charge disproportionation is the key to the electronic localization in nickelates.

the charge disproportionation in TmNiNi3O6 is accompanied by the formation of the NiO4 square plaquettes with the Ni3+ cation in a high spin state (t2g4eg1) and the Ni3+ in a low spin state (t 2g6) and the NiO6 octahedron with the Ni3 + cation in a low spin (t 2 g6) state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in both compounds the 57Fe hyperfine field is reduced by about 20% at T > TIM and TN.
the hyperfine interactions in the studied nickelates are sensitive to the charge ordering in the range of temperature transitions of insulator ↔ metal.
the charge disproportionation is a common phenomenon in nickelates with different rare-earth ions.
